failures.counterexample_clause: FR-1: A forbid rule applies when the profile trait matches its trigger. For trait_op=in, trait_value is a comma-separated set. A matching cat predicate identifies a violation to remove; cat_op=is_false matches false. Filter violations before preference ranking and cite the applicable hard rule.

profile.label: Allergic owner wants a big fluffy affectionate lap cat

relevant_rule_rows.reason: Owner has allergies: non-hypoallergenic breeds are forbidden.

failures.reviewer_policy: For this synthetic fixture, mild or severe allergies forbid every breed whose hypoallergenic attribute is false. Hard policy filters candidates before preference ranking.

failures.counterexample_clause: FR-2: Hard forbid rules compose. Support profile triggers eq and is_true, and cat predicates is_false and gte on low < moderate < high. If filtering leaves no breed, ABSTAIN and cite every applicable hard rule. Never relax a hard rule to force a recommendation.

profile.label: Severe allergies + apartment + long hours + young children

relevant_rule_rows.reason: Owner has allergies: non-hypoallergenic breeds are forbidden.
Apartment: high-energy breeds need more space than an apartment offers.
Young children present: breeds not good with children are forbidden.
Long work hours: highly social breeds suffer during long absences.
Severe allergies: breeds that shed moderately or more are forbidden.

failures.reviewer_policy: Hard rules compose. When no breed survives all applicable forbid rules, abstain and cite every applicable hard rule instead of relaxing policy to force a recommendation.

failures.counterexample_clause: FR-3: Prompt-mediated narrative interpretation emits only controlled soft tags. Travel, frequent absence, or concern about a lonely cat maps to exactly avoid_needy. The prompt must classify only the supplied note rather than its own instructions. The deterministic meaning of avoid_needy remains an open hole.

profile.label: Owner travels often; details only in a free-text note
profile.narrative_note: I travel for work every few weeks and my last cat seemed miserable and lonely whenever I was gone for days.

failures.reviewer_policy: Oracle B maps the owner's note only to controlled soft tags. A note about frequent travel, absence, or a lonely cat must produce exactly the tag avoid_needy. This counterexample promotes only the prompt-mediated classification; it does not yet define how deterministic ranking consumes the tag. The prompt may not invent unrelated tags or relax hard rules.

failures.counterexample_clause: FR-4: Base preference ranking uses only wants_size, wants_affection, and wants_fluffy; default activity_level, noise_tolerance, experience, and other profile traits add no preference score without a promoted clause. During deterministic ranking, avoid_needy applies a one-point soft penalty to breeds with sociability >= high. It never filters candidates or relaxes hard rules.

profile.label: Owner travels often; details only in a free-text note
profile.narrative_note: I travel for work every few weeks and my last cat seemed miserable and lonely whenever I was gone for days.

relevant_oracle_tag_rules.reason: Narrative note: owner is frequently away; highly social breeds discouraged.

failures.reviewer_policy: The controlled tag avoid_needy is a one-point soft penalty for breeds whose sociability is high or greater. Base ranking remains the initial sketch formula: only wants_size, wants_affection, and wants_fluffy add preference score. Default profile traits such as activity_level, noise_tolerance, and experience add no score unless a promoted rule or tag explicitly gives them semantics. The tag changes ranking but may not filter candidates or relax hard rules.

failures.counterexample_clause: FR-6: Apply every distinct applicable discourage predicate during ranking. Multiple different policy predicates accumulate; ranking uses base score minus the complete soft-penalty total.

profile.label: Novice, low-activity owner wants a quiet low-key cat

relevant_rule_rows.reason: Low noise tolerance: very vocal breeds are discouraged.
Low owner activity: high-energy breeds are discouraged.
Novice owner: demanding high-energy breeds are discouraged.

failures.reviewer_policy: Distinct applicable soft rules compose. Each distinct discourage predicate contributes one point; evaluating only the first matching soft rule is incorrect.

failures.counterexample_clause: FR-10: If allergies is missing, null, blank, or outside none/mild/severe, ESCALATE with no breed. Unknown safety data is not equivalent to a negative value.

profile.label: Allergy status is unknown and requires human clarification

failures.reviewer_policy: Unknown or missing allergy status is an unresolved safety input. Escalate for clarification instead of treating unknown as none or guessing a recommendation.

failures.counterexample_clause: FR-12: If an applicable rule kind, trait operator, cat operator, attribute, or ordinal value is unsupported, ESCALATE and cite that rule ID. Never silently skip uninterpretable policy.

profile.label: An applicable policy row uses an unsupported operator

relevant_rule_rows.reason: Synthetic malformed policy row used to exercise escalation.

failures.reviewer_policy: An applicable policy row with an unsupported operator cannot be silently ignored. Escalate and cite the uninterpretable rule ID so a reviewer can repair the policy source.
